pr.title: Let a request carry a start action the person presses start for
pr.head: e7609e49ab83d4fa60dc7805c3e968acdb7687cb

summary: Projector's inbox lets an agent post items to the person through the panel above the Claude Code prompt. Layer 1 (#372) added a request, work only the person can do, which they mark done or decline. This layer, layer 2 of the plan docs/projects/inbox/requests, adds a start action: one line saying what the agent does before the person can begin, such as installing a build on their phone.

1. The agent posts a request with a start action, through project inbox request --start or the request tool's start.
  2. The person presses start on 8 in the request's drawer. The panel runs project inbox start <n> --action <the action the drawer shows>, which refuses with exit 65 when the agent has revised the action since, so the press consents to exactly what was read.
  3. The deliverer sends STARTED <n> <request> → <action> through the same claim and settle path that delivers answers.
  4. The agent does the action and marks the request ready, or blocked with a reason, through new ready and block tools. A blocked request offers retry, which records a new start.

start joins the permission ask rules so an agent can't consent for the person, and the plan is marked completed. The agents block moves to version 20, which also tells agents to build ahead so that a start is quick. Reviews of earlier heads found three problems: type errors in the new tests, tool results that didn't mention STARTED, and an over-long line in the agents block. Later commits fixed all three, and no finding is open at this head.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• start action: the request's start field, one line the person reads before pressing start.
  • started: { action, startedAt, deliveredAt? }, the action as it read at the press, and when STARTED reached the agent.
  • progress: { state, reason?, at }, the agent's ready or blocked.
  • owed line: the next message an item owes its agent, answer, restored, or started.
  • claim: a deliverer's hold on an owed line, which now records which line it took.

groups.title: The start in the inbox store and the CLI
groups.kicker: Three new commands, and a claim that remembers which line it took
intro: A request now stores start, started, and progress. start records the person's press, refusing an action that differs from the stored one; ready and block record the agent's progress and refuse a request that isn't started.

A STARTED is a second line a request can owe while it stays open, beside restoredAt. owed_line picks the next one, and claim records it on the claim as line, so settle finishes the right line even when an outcome lands between the claim and the settle.

checks.text: Reproduced in a scratch store at this head: a stale --action exits 65 and records nothing; start exits 65 on a request without a start action, a question, a notice, a resolved request, and a second press; ready and block exit 65 before a start; retry after a block takes the same --action guard.

files.note: The start's lifecycle: start, report for ready and blocked, reset_start on revise and restore, and the claim's recorded line.

checks.text: The order matters: an undelivered answer first, then word of a restore, then an open request's undelivered start.

A claimed STARTED keeps its claim when an outcome or withdrawal lands; an unclaimed one is removed. Reproduced both: a decline during a claimed STARTED is delivered after it settles, and a withdrawal sends nothing.
Any revision of a request, even of its detail alone, returns it to open and drops a claim on its STARTED; a deliverer holding that claim then fails its settle on the token.
The consent guard. Both sides are stripped, and a mismatch exits 65 without writing.

StartTests walk the CLI lifecycle and the claim ordering.

groups.title: Only the person presses start
groups.kicker: start joins the ask rules; ready and block run freely
intro: An agent that could run project inbox start could consent to its own start action, so start joins answer, dismiss, snooze, done, and decline among Claude Code's ask rules and stays out of Codex's allowed list. The panel runs it itself, so a press in the panel never asks. People take the new rule by running project init again.

groups.title: The drawer, the deliverer, and the tools
groups.kicker: start on 8, a stage mark on the line, and the ready and block tools
intro: The drawer of a request with a start action shows Start: and the action, and offers start request on 8, a digit an open request leaves free. A press passes the action the drawer shows. On exit 65 the panel drops its listing so the next check reads the store and redraws the new action. The line then ends with starting, ready, or blocked, and a blocked request offers retry request on the same key.
The deliverer treats an undelivered start like any owed line. When a STARTED cannot be delivered, reopen removes the start and a toast asks the person to press start again.

groups.title: What every agent reads
groups.kicker: Agents block version 20 teaches the start action
intro: The generated block in every repository's agent instructions now tells an agent to give a start action only when it must prepare something first, and to do the slow part, such as a build, before it posts the request. The agent then acts only once STARTED arrives, does exactly what that message quotes, and marks the request ready or blocked. The request tool's description says the same.
